extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, patent agents, patentees, and IP lawyers/practitioners (United Kingdom)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for requesting and opposing amendments to specifications, applying for extensions of patents, compulsory licences, registration and related fees under the Patents (Designs) Act 1883 and accompanying rules. Covers forms, timelines, evidentiary steps, limits on amendment, and criteria the Judicial Committee/Board will apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for enlargement of time for payment
rubrics_metrics.description: The enlargement of time, where granted, is subject to the conditions — (1) That a fee be paid; (2) That it be for not more than three months; (3) That where acts of infringement are committed between the expiration of the prescribed time for payment and the enlargement thereof, the Court, in an action for infringement, may refuse to give damages for such acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for extension of time (Form K) and substantiation
rubrics_metrics.description: The application for extension is to be in Form K (Patents Forms), and the circumstances under which the patentee failed by accident, mistake, or inadvertence to make the payment, must be stated in detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comptroller may require the facts alleged to be substantiated (Patents Rules, 46).

rubrics_metrics.name: How to request amendment of a specification
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant or a patentee may, from time to time, by request in writing left at the patent office, seek leave to amend his specification, including drawings forming part thereof, by way of disclaimer, correction, or explanation, stating the nature of such amendment and his reasons for the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Statutory reference: sect. 18.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement and opposition period for proposed amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: The request and the nature of such proposed amendment shall be advertised in the prescribed manner, and at any time within one month from its first advertisement any person may give notice at the patent office of opposition to the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (See Patents Rules for prescribed advertisement.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller duty on opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Where such notice is given, the comptroller shall give notice of the opposition to the person making the request, and shall hear and decide the case, subject to an appeal to the law officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law officer's role on appeals or hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: The law officer shall, if required, hear the person making the request and the person so giving notice, and being in the opinion of the law officer entitled to be heard in opposition to the request, and shall determine whether and subject to what conditions, if any, the amendment ought to be allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If leave to amend is refused by the comptroller, the person making the request may appeal to the law officer; the law officer may hear the person and the comptroller and make an order determining the amendment and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller determination when no opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no notice of opposition is given, or the person so giving notice does not appear, the comptroller shall determine whether and subject to what conditions, if any, the amendment ought to be allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: No amendment that enlarges or substantially changes the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment shall be allowed that would make the specification, as amended, claim an invention substantially larger than or substantially different from the invention claimed by the specification as it stood before amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Statutory safeguard limiting scope of allowable amendments.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave to amend conclusive (except fraud)
rubrics_metrics.description: Leave to amend shall be conclusive as to the right of the party to make the amendment allowed, except in case of fraud; and the amendment shall in all Courts and for all purposes be deemed to form part of the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment not allowed during pending legal proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The foregoing provisions of this section do not apply when and so long as any action for infringement or other legal proceeding in relation to a patent is pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and effect of a disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: The object of a disclaimer is to enable a patentee to omit those parts of a specification which, if retained, would make the patent void. The disclaimer operates to strike out the parts of the specification disclaimed and does not serve to explain what is left; the disclaimer will be deemed part of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A disclaimer is not retrospective so as to make a person liable for infringement prior to the disclaimer unless the patentee establishes to the satisfaction of the Court that his original claim was framed in good faith and with reasonable skill and knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content requirements for amendment application (practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for leave to amend is made in Form F (Patent Forms). The reasons for making the amendment are to be stated, and the nature of the proposed amendment is to be shown in red ink on a copy of the original specification and drawings which are to accompany the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application requires a 30s. stamp if the patent has not been sealed, if sealed a £1 stamp (see Schedule to Patents Rules). The application will be advertised in the Official Journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of opposition — Form and required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of opposition to the amendment may be given in Form G (Patents Forms). The grounds of opposition are to be stated, an address for service in the United Kingdom is to be given, and the opponent himself must sign the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice requires a 10s. stamp and is to be accompanied by an unstamped copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit exchange timetable for amendment opposition hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Within fourteen days after the expiration of one month from the first advertisement of the application, the opponent is to leave at the Patent Office affidavits in support of his opposition and deliver a list to the applicant. Copies of such affidavits may be obtained by the applicant; within fourteen days from delivery of the list the applicant is to leave his affidavits in answer and deliver a list to the opponent; the opponent is allowed seven days to leave his affidavits in reply and deliver a list to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No further evidence is allowed except by leave of the comptroller, obtained (a) on written consent of both parties, or (b) specially, after notice to the other side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing notice and fees for amendment oppositions
rubrics_metrics.description: The comptroller gives both parties seven days' notice of the hearing. A hearing fee of £1 has to be paid by both parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When leave to amend is given the comptroller may require new specification and drawings to be left (Patents Rules, 54). The amendment is also advertised (Patents Rules, 56).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when leave to amend is given
rubrics_metrics.description: When leave to amend is given the comptroller may require new specification and drawings to be left and the amendment is advertised in the Official Journal; the appeal from the decision to the law officer is governed by the usual rules as to appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Patents Rules 48–56 for detailed procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court power to permit amendment during action
rubrics_metrics.description: In an action for infringement or in a proceeding for revocation the Court or a judge may at any time order that the patentee shall, subject to such terms as to costs and otherwise as the Court or a judge may impose, be at liberty to apply at the Patent Office for leave to amend his specification by way of disclaimer, and may direct that in the meantime the trial or hearing of the action shall be postponed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the Court makes an order an official or verified copy of such order is to be left at the Patent Office along with the application for leave (Patents Rules, 55). The fee on application is 3s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction of damages for prior use after amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment by way of disclaimer, correction, or explanation has been allowed, no damages shall be given in any action in respect of the use of the invention before the disclaimer, correction, or explanation, unless the patentee establishes to the satisfaction of the Court that his original claim was framed in good faith and with reasonable skill and knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction means amendment may affect remedies for prior acts; patentees should consider whether to amend during proceedings as it can forfeit damages unless the good faith/skill standard is met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising requirement for every amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Every amendment of a specification shall be advertised in the prescribed manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The advertisement will be in the Official Journal of the Patent Office and in any other manner if the comptroller so directs (Patents Rules, 66).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for compulsory licences (Board of Trade)
rubrics_metrics.description: If on petition it is proved to the Board of Trade that by reason of the default of a patentee to grant licences on reasonable terms — (a) The patent is not being worked in the United Kingdom; or (b) The reasonable requirements of the public with respect to the invention cannot be supplied; or (c) Any person is prevented from working or using to the best advantage an invention of which he is possessed — the Board may order the patentee to grant licences on such terms as the Board deems just.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such order may be enforced by mandamus. The Board will regard the nature of the invention and circumstances of the case in determining terms (royalties, security for payment, or otherwise).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and temporal application of compulsory licence provision
rubrics_metrics.description: This section applies only to letters patent granted on applications made after the 31st Dec. 1883, and does not affect (1) patents granted before that date, or (2) patents granted after that date on applications made previous to such date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application and petition practice for compulsory licences
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is made in Form H; a petition is framed in Form Hi stating the title of the invention, the petitioner's interest, the grounds relied on with reference to those mentioned in the section, the circumstances showing default of the patentee, and the purport of the order asked for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application, with duplicate copies and the petition accompanied by affidavits or other evidence, are left at the Patent Office. If a prima facie case is made, the Board will give directions; the petitioner must deliver copies to the patentee and the patentee has 14 days to give notice in Form I (stamped) if he intends to oppose and to leave affidavits in opposition; the petitioner then has 14 days to leave affidavits in reply. Further proceedings fixed by Board (Patents Rules, 57–63).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandamus to enforce Board orders
rubrics_metrics.description: An order of the Board of Trade directing the patentee to grant licences may be enforced by mandamus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rules Supreme Court, 1883, Order LIII as to enforcement by mandamus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register of Patents — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be kept at the Patent Office a Register of Patents where shall be entered the names and addresses of grantees of patents, notifications of assignments and of transmissions of patents, of licences under patents, and of amendments, extensions, and revocations of patents, and such other matters affecting the validity or proprietorship of patents as may from time to time be prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register as prima facie evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The register of patents shall be prima facie evidence of any matters by this Act directed or authorised to be inserted therein.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents to be supplied for registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of deeds, licences, and any other documents affecting the proprietorship in any letters patent or in any licence thereunder must be supplied to the comptroller in the prescribed manner for filing in the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents Rules specify forms and manner (see Patents Rules, 68, 74).

rubrics_metrics.name: No trusts entered on the register
rubrics_metrics.description: No trust, express, implied, or constructive, is to be entered on the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Sect. 28 — 'Trusts not entered.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of patentee's name/address/title on sealing
rubrics_metrics.description: The name, address, and description of the patentee, together with the title of the invention is entered on the register by the comptroller upon the sealing of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Patents Rules, 64.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to register assignment/transmission (Form L) and required evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person becomes entitled to a patent or any share or interest therein by assignment, transmission or operation of law, a request for entry of his name in the register as such proprietor is to be addressed to the comptroller in Form L, bearing a 10s. stamp. The request must state particulars of the assignment, transmission, or other operation of law so as to show the manner in which the patent or share have become vested in him; the assignment or other document must be forwarded along with an examined copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the document is a matter of record, an official or certified copy is to be left (Patents Rules, 65–69). Evidence examples: probate for wills, letters of administration for intestacy, bankruptcy certificate for trustee's title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of licences (Form M) and fee requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of licences application for registration is to be made in Form M, stamped with the prescribed stamp; the original licence and an examined copy must accompany the application (Patents Rules, 74).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments will be entered by the comptroller; the fee is paid on application (see sect. 18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of revocation orders and Privy Council orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The person in whose favour the order is made is to leave at the Patent Office an office copy of the order of revocation, when the purport of such order will be registered. Application for entry of an order of the Privy Council is to be made in Form S, stamped with a 10s. stamp, accompanied by an office copy of the order (Patents Rules, 71).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreements affecting patent interests should be registered
rubrics_metrics.description: All agreements by which a person acquires any interest in a patent ought to be registered: application being made as in the case of an assignment (Patents Rules, 65).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of register entry on powers of person entered
rubrics_metrics.description: By sect. 87 the person whose name is entered in the register has, subject to any rights appearing from the register to be vested in other persons, power absolutely to assign or grant licences as to, or otherwise deal with the same and to give effectual receipts for any consideration for such assignment, licence, or dealing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Power is given to enforce any equities in respect of such patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees payable under the Act and rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees shall be paid in respect of the several instruments described in the second schedule to this Act, and such fees shall be levied and paid to the Exchequer. The Board of Trade may, with consent of the Treasury, reduce any of those fees from time to time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The complete list of fees payable will be found in the first schedule to the Patents Rules. Specific reductions (e.g., provisional protection and first payment) are noted in the text and schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee petition for extension of term — timing and advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee may, after advertising in manner directed by any rules made under the section his intention to do so, present a petition to Her Majesty in Council praying that his patent may be extended for a further term; such petition must be presented at least six months before the time limited for the expiration of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (No rules had yet been made when text written.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to enter caveat against extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may enter a caveat, addressed to the Registrar of the Council at the Council Office, against the extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial Committee criteria for considering extension petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Judicial Committee shall, in considering their decision, have regard to the nature and merits of the invention in relation to the public, to the profits made by the patentee as such, and to all the circumstances of the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible outcomes of extension petition
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Judicial Committee report that the patentee has been inadequately remunerated by his patent, it shall be lawful for Her Majesty in Council to extend the term of the patent for a further term not exceeding seven, or in exceptional cases fourteen years; or to order the grant of a new patent for the term therein mentioned, and containing any restrictions, conditions, and provisions the Committee may think fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs and procedural rules for extension petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall be lawful for Her Majesty in Council to make rules of procedure and practice for regulating proceedings on such petitions; the costs of all parties of and incident to such proceedings shall be in the discretion of the Judicial Committee; orders respecting costs shall be enforceable as if they were orders of a Division of the High Court of Justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher utility standard for extension than for patent grant
rubrics_metrics.description: In considering the merits of the invention for extension, the Judicial Committee require a greater degree of utility to be shown than is necessary in order to obtain a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: granting an extension demands stronger proof of public benefit; extensions will be refused where utility is small or detrimental to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-use raises presumption against utility (rebuttable)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that the invention has not been carried into practice so as to benefit the public will raise a strong presumption against its utility; this presumption may be rebutted by showing that the nature of the invention was such that it would not likely come into immediate use, or that non-use was due to the pecuniary difficulties of the patentee, or that the market was limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong and unanswered evidence of utility may be sufficient even if not tested by actual employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profits to be considered: include licences/royalties and foreign/export profits
rubrics_metrics.description: In estimating profits the applicant must include all profits made by him as patentee, such as result from licences or royalties, including profits made in another country or made by sale for exportation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See authorities cited (e.g. In re Johnson's Patent; In re Hardy's Patent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Profits made by manufacturing not generally included
rubrics_metrics.description: Profits made by the patentee not 'as such' — e.g., by manufacturing the patent article — would under the subsection not be included when estimating patentee profits for extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee will not go behind accounts to separate what part of profits are as manufacturer and what as patentee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deductions allowable from profits when assessing remuneration
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant is allowed to make certain deductions, e.g., expenses incurred in bringing out the patent; expenses in making experiments; in defending the patent; in bringing the invention into use; a sum for exclusive devotion of time in bringing the patent into notice; and a manufacturer's fair profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law examples include In re Roberts' Patent, In re Kay's Patent, In re Galloway's Patent, In re Carr's Patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other circumstances: personal merit, skill and ingenuity of inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: The Judicial Committee have been accustomed to look at other circumstances including the personal merit of the inventor and the skill and ingenuity shown by the patentee in making the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal merit is distinct from public utility; cases are cited where merit attributed to inventor for skill shown (In re Daumton's Patent; In re Whitehouse's Patent; In re Hill's Patent).
